To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
bit stream programming can be done in a declarative, memory-safe, and efficient way in Erlang.

(i) bit stream programming in Erlang is a viable approach for writing high-performance applications that manipulate bit streams and (ii) this programming style is more succinct, less error prone and totally memory safe compared to low-level languages such C.

(1) high-level bit stream programming is possible in Erlang, (2) the performance is competitive to that of other functional languages and to that of C, (3) the implementation of bit stream comprehensions is non-trivial, and (4) bit stream comprehensions can be implemented in a memory-safe manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How to make bit stream programming easier and safer?
the following questions: (i) Can high-level bit stream programming be implemented efficiently?
the design and implementation of a bit stream programming language that is both declarative and high-level, and at the same time has good performance characteristics.

bit streams are a good fit for functional programming.
bit stream programming in Erlang is a very efficient and effective way to solve bit stream processing problems.
Erlang bit stream programming is a very good alternative to C bit stream programming, and that Erlang is a good alternative to C in general.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bit stream comprehensions are a powerful, high-level construct that is well suited for bit stream programming, and that it is possible to implement them with good performance.
bit stream programming in Erlang is a viable alternative to bit twiddling in C, and in fact, in many situations, it is the better choice.
bit stream programming in Erlang is a viable and efficient approach to a variety of applications.

bit stream programming can be made easier and safer without sacrificing performance.
